subject: Request: SDLC change-control & merge policy artifacts for SIG assessment
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@northbridge-risk.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG follow-up: change-control and merge policy artifacts

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As discussed, the assessor team needs a small artifact bundle showing how merge approvals, CI role restrictions, and emergency change procedures are enforced in production-bound codepaths. At minimum we need: 1) current merge policy (including approval matrix); 2) sample CI run with approval gates and the permission set for the pipeline runner; and 3) a short chronology showing a recent emergency change and the rollforward/rollback notes.

Can you confirm whether you can provide these artifacts by EOD Monday (2026-08-31)? Also let us know if any items are sensitive and should be sent via SFTP/secure link rather than inline.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Patel
Senior Assessor, Northbridge Risk Assessors

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@northbridge-risk.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: change-control and merge policy artifacts

Maya —

We can provide the artifacts. Quick notes up front so you know what to expect:
- Merge policy is our canonical doc (PDF) and includes required approvers by area, the automated checks (lint, unit/integration tests), and the blocking branch protection rules.
- CI pipeline permission matrix is exported from our pipeline service (CSV) showing the service account scopes and who can trigger protected runs.
- For emergency changes, we include a short chronology + postmortem fragment (redacted PII) showing the approval path and the rollback tag.

Attachments will be delivered via a secure Drive link; the CI permissions CSV contains internal IAM IDs, so we will redact service-account tokens and provide the IDs rather than keys. If you need raw logs we can arrange an SFTP transfer with our security team.

Irene — can you assemble the artifacts (merge_policy, ci_pipeline_permissions, chronology) and upload to the secure Drive share? Lauren — please confirm the redaction step for the CI export so we do not leak tokens.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Platform Security, Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Maya Patel <maya.patel@northbridge-risk.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-30T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: change-control and merge policy artifacts

>

> - Merge policy is our canonical doc (PDF) and includes required approvers by area, the automated checks (lint, unit/integration tests), and the blocking branch protection rules.
> - CI pipeline permission matrix is exported from our pipeline service (CSV) showing the service account scopes and who can trigger protected runs.
> - For emergency changes, we include a short chronology + postmortem fragment (redacted PII) showing the approval path and the rollback tag.
> 
> Attachments will be delivered via a secure Drive link; the CI permissions CSV contains internal IAM IDs, so we will redact service-account tokens and provide the IDs rather than keys. If you need raw logs we can arrange an SFTP transfer with our security team.

Hi all — attaching the Drive bundle stub and a short note on redaction. Items uploaded: redwood_merge_policy_v2.1.pdf, ci_pipeline_permissions.csv (IAM IDs only), change-approval-chronology-2025-2026.csv.

Redaction summary: we removed ephemeral tokens, replaced service-account emails with role IDs (svc-role-###), and removed user PII from the chronology. All artifacts are watermarked and read-only; link shared with Northbridge assessor group. If you need a signed attest to the redaction, I can route to security-compliance for (SOC2) attestation.

Attachments: [redwood_merge_policy_v2.1.pdf] [ci_pipeline_permissions.csv] [change-approval-chronology-2025-2026.csv]

Irene Choi
Director, Compliance Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@northbridge-risk.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-31T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: change-control and merge policy artifacts

Thanks — received the Drive bundle and the redaction note. Quick clarifying Qs from the assessor team after a first pass:

1) The merge policy PDF references a "fast-track emergency approval" flow. Can you provide the short checklist the on-call follows when invoking fast-track? We just need the decision criteria and the minimum approvers.
2) In the CI CSV the pipeline runner shows a cross-project role (svc-runner-x). Please confirm whether that role can modify production IAM bindings or only execute pre-authorized deploy steps.
3) For the chronology row dated 2026-03-14 there is a rollback tag but no explicit post-rollback verification note. Can you either add the verification step or point us to the run ID where the verification occurred?

If you can answer these items inline or update the chronology CSV (a single row) that would close our open asks. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Maya
